pr_body:
This PR fixes #4123 

## Problem

SetValue was only using PhysicalType, causing types that carry ExtraTypeInfo that might be relevant in casting to not convert properly, because the cast is not performed.
After changing this to comparing the entire LogicalType, I found that there are casts missing for types that share the same physical type, which makes sense because those should never need to be cast, so I don't compare LogicalTypeId anymore.

Then I discovered that GetValue does not properly inherit `alias` ExtraTypeInfo, and I figured that's probably irrelevant to casting, so I stopped comparing alias to determine if a cast should happen.
Which resulted in this:

```sql
SQL Query
SELECT add_point(({'x': 2, 'y': 3})::POINT, ({'x': 3, 'y': 4})::POINT)
================================================================================
Actual result:
Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'add_point(STRUCT(x INTEGER, y INTEGER), STRUCT(x INTEGER, y INTEGER))'. You might need to add explicit type casts.
        Candidate functions:
        add_point(POINT, POINT) -> POINT
```

It seems `alias` *is* relevant when casting.
This previously succeeded because no cast was performed, since POINT and STRUCT share a PhysicalType (not entirely sure still why this did not work anymore when I stopped comparing the alias)

## Changes

I eventually landed on adding the type_info of the Vector to all Values that come out of Vector::GetValue.
If there are other places this becomes relevant (Value inheriting a LogicalType) it might be better to handle this by adding an optional `const LogicalType &type` parameter to all Value constructors.

issue_context.title: Vector::SetValue not always casting when it should
issue_context.body:
#### What happens?
When determining whether or not to cast, SetValue only considers PhysicalType.
This can be problematic in case there is additional type_info present on the LogicalType.
(For a comprehensive list of the possible TypeInfo see PR #1851)

An example I came across is DECIMAL ignoring the width/scale, producing wrong results by not casting if the width/scale differ.
I have attempted to fix the issue by always comparing the LogicalTypes using the equality operator but this caused enough issues to demand a separate PR.  
So for now there is only a simple band aid fix targeting DECIMAL.

#### To Reproduce
There's not really a reproducible example to this issue, it's more a potential problem that should be addressed.
Since this has caused issues with DECIMAL, there's a high probability other issues could arise from this.

#### Notes
When attempting to patch this potential issue I have observed two (semi) big hurdles.
1. Value::CastAs(LogicalType& target_type) is not inheriting collation when target_type is VARCHAR, which caused this to infinite recurse:
```c++
	if (val.type() != GetType()) {
		SetValue(index, val.CastAs(GetType()));
		return;
	}
```
2. When not just comparing using `PhysicalType` but instead comparing using `LogicalTypeId` a lot of tests break that relied on there never needing to be an actual Cast performed if the PhysicalType was the same, such as:
```
Invalid Input Error: Failed to cast value: Unimplemented type for cast (BIGINT -> TIMESTAMP)
```

The second issue is only relevant if there is a difference in the way that data should be represented between two LogicalType's that share the same PhysicalType. To which I unfortunately don't know the answer yet.
comments: Issues I was facing are likely caused by missing support for the ALIAS `ExtraTypeInfo` introduced by PR #3668

The issue is highlighted by this test:

```sql
statement ok
CREATE TYPE alias AS VARCHAR;

statement ok
CREATE TABLE test AS select 'happy'::ALIAS;
```

When we force a cast, this causes the following assertion to be triggered:
```
TransactionContext Error: Failed to commit: INTERNAL Error: Assertion triggered in file "duckdb/src/common/types/vector.cpp" on line 94: other.GetType() == GetType()
```

~~Currently on master, Vector::SetValue does not cast when the physical types are the same, but when we force a cast, this issue arises.~~
despite hitting an assertion, the query completes succesfully on release
